title: No bail for alleged Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of Australia’s ‘febrile’ political environment
byline: Caitlin Cassidy; Henry Belot; Benita Kolovos
paragraphs: The head of the Australian federal police has condemned a “febrile” political environment that has seen one person charged every week over the alleged threatening of MPs, as Victoria announces new steps to protect politicians.

But the AFP and Victoria police insist they had no intelligence to suggest 43-year-old Brendan Nugent would go on to allegedly drive a Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP Helen Haines in a targeted attack.

Haines had one leg amputated after the alleged attack. Doctors had worked to save her second leg, but it was also amputated, her husband, Phil Haines, said at a press conference on Wednesday. Haines was in a stable condition, he said.
